speaker: (the host)
text: Supper and a bed. Fourteen pence. The bed is shared, and the house is full of other men's boots.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fourteen pence. I'll see the bed when I've eaten, and I won't praise it before that.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Twenty-one miles. He sat ten of them and walked the rest, and he has been not-glad the whole way, which is how I know the back has had the right of it.

speaker: (the host)
text: The dog has the stool in the yard. You may have the bench, or you may argue with the dog. The dog has won that argument all summer.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Let the dog have the stool. A man who has done twenty-one miles does not need a stool to prove he has arrived.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fourteen pence covers supper and the bed. It does not cover a speech about the miles. The miles were his pace, and I kept it.

speaker: (the host)
text: Bacon, and bread, and the bed after. You will not get a better account of it by standing in the yard.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: We will eat. He will sleep on the side that lets him rise. If your fourteen pence grows while we are eating, say so before the bacon is gone.

speaker: (the host)
text: It will not grow. Fourteen was fourteen last month, and the dearth has not yet learned to count beds.
